standard_prerequisites.name: Depth computed from the fibre and the base
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked at the start of the counted proof (lines 46633-46640)
standard_prerequisites.use: Expresses the depth of the localised ring as the sum of the fibre contribution and the depth of the base local ring.

standard_prerequisites.name: Dimension of the localised ring compared with the base and the fibre
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the inequality between the dimension of the local ring and the two pieces it splits into.

core_obligations: For a prime of the target lying over a prime of the base, use the depth formula to write the depth of the localised ring in terms of the fibre and the base (proof lines 46632-46645).
Compare that with the dimension of the localised ring using the S_k hypotheses on the fibre and on the base, and conclude the S_k inequality for the target (proof lines 46645-46673).
proof_roadmap: Express depth through the fibre and the base (proof lines 46632-46645).
Combine the two S_k hypotheses into the inequality for the target (proof lines 46645-46674).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that Serre's condition S_k ascends along a flat map of Noetherian rings whose fibre rings satisfy S_k, provided the base does (statement lines 46619-46630). The proof does not reprove the depth formula: it invokes the comparison of depth with the fibre and the base, then estimates the dimension of the localised ring from the two parts and applies the two hypotheses to obtain the required inequality (proof lines 46632-46674). Deciding how to split both depth and dimension between the fibre and the base is the content. H2.
